'''''Chamaedorea seifrizii''''', commonly known as '''bamboo palm''', '''parlor palm''', or '''reed palm''', is a species of plant in the family [[Arecaceae]]. It is a subtropical palm that grows up to 20 feet tall, and is commonly used as a houseplant.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Chamaedorea seifrizii'' (Bamboo Palm, Parlor Palm, Reed Palm) |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/chamaedorea-seifrizii/ |website=North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |publisher=[[North Carolina State University]] and [[North Carolina A&T State University]] |access-date=17 April 2022}}</ref> The evergreen leaves are pinnately divided, and yellow flowers are borne on a panicle.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Chamaedorea seifrizii'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/46437/bamboo-palm/details |publisher=[[Royal Horticultural Society]] |access-date=17 April 2022 |language=en-gb}}</ref> The fruit are small, round, and black.<ref name=FNA/>

==Taxonomy and history==
''Chamaedorea seifrizii'' was described in 1938 by German botanist [[Max Burret]] based on a [[type specimen]] collected near [[Chichén Itzá]] in [[Mexico]]. Burret named the species in honour of [[William Seifriz]], the collector of the type material. The holotype has since been lost, but a neotype was designated by Donald R. Hodel in 1992 and is now stored in the [[Liberty Hyde Bailey|Liberty Hyde Bailey Hortorium]].<ref name=PW>{{cite web |title=''Chamaedorea seifrizii'' Burret, Notizbl. Bot. Gart. Berlin-Dahlem 14: 268 (1938) |url=https://www.palmweb.org/cdm_dataportal/taxon/0ea57d2c-2fcd-484f-82fc-5aba11f48e7f |website=Palmweb |access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref><ref name=BH>{{cite journal |last1=Reveal |first1=James L. |last2=Nixon |first2=Kevin C. |author-link1=James L. Reveal |year=2013 |title=The palm type collection in the Liberty Hyde Bailey Hortorium (BH) |journal=Phytoneuron |volume=2013-79 |page=15 |issn=2153-733X |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/43398425 |via=[[Biodiversity Heritage Library]]}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''C. seifrizii'' is native to [[Belize]] ([[Belize District]], [[Cayo District]], [[Corozal District]], and [[Orange Walk District]]), [[Guatemala]] ([[Petén Department]]), [[Honduras]] (mainland and [[Islas de la Bahia]]), and [[Mexico]] ([[Campeche]], [[Quintana Roo]], [[Tabasco]], and [[Yucatán]]). It can be found at elevations of up to {{cvt|500|m}}, often on [[limestone]] outcrops. It grows in moist woodlands and forests, including disturbed habitat.<ref name=IUCN/><ref name=PW/>

It occurs as an [[introduced species]] in [[Florida, United States]].<ref name=FNA>{{cite web |last1=Zona |first1=Scott |title=''Chamaedorea seifrizii''|url=http://floranorthamerica.org/Chamaedorea_seifrizii |website=[[Flora of North America]] |access-date=31 July 2024}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
Referred to as {{lang|myn|xate}}, {{lang|myn|xiat}}, or {{lang|myn|chiat}} in [[Mayan languages|Mayan]], ''C. seifrizii'' was cultivated by the [[Maya people]] in the [[pre-Columbian era]] as an [[ornamental plant]] and possibly for religious purposes, often being planted around villages and temples.<ref name=PW/>

Today, ''C. seifrizii'' is widely cultivated as both an indoor and outdoor plant.<ref name=PW/> It is easily propagated from seed or by [[Division (horticulture)|division]].<ref name=DLJ>{{cite book |last1=Jones |first1=David L. |author-link1=David L. Jones (botanist) |year=1995 |title=Palms Throughout the World |publisher=[[Smithsonian Institution Press]] |page=178 |isbn=1-56098-616-6 |lccn=95068615 |oclc=33124561}}</ref>
